name: WizardLM: Empowering Large Pre-Trained Language Models to Follow Complex Instructions
problem: Instruction-following data is expensive to hand-write, and humans struggle to produce the high-complexity instructions that actually teach a model.
mechanism: Evol-Instruct: iteratively REWRITE a seed instruction into progressively more complex ones (add constraints, deepen reasoning, concretize), producing a difficulty-graded instruction corpus without human authors. The generated instructions are mixed and used to fine-tune LLaMA. The method is a DATA-generation method, not an architecture change - which is why it composes with whatever base model you have.
speedup_reported: Paper's own claim (abstract): human evaluation on a complexity-balanced testbed and Vicuna's testset shows Evol-Instruct instructions are SUPERIOR TO HUMAN-CREATED ONES; on the high-complexity subset WizardLM outputs are PREFERRED TO OPENAI CHATGPT; and in GPT-4 automatic evaluation WizardLM achieves 'more than 90% capacity of ChatGPT on 17 out of 29 skills'. The 17/29 is the honest headline - on 12 of 29 skills it did NOT reach 90% of ChatGPT. COMPRESSION RATIO: not applicable. QUALITY COST: a self-judged score against ChatGPT, with both the judge (GPT-4) and the baseline proprietary.
